title: Assemble the tools offered to an agent
summary: Build a toolbox from the verified Luc set and any unmigrated native compatibility tools. Libraries are checked before Skills; unavailable rows accompany the three wrappers; use_skill appears only with ready reads.

replaceability.why: Assembly decides which Lucs reach the agent: it applies the Luc set, safe mode and the stand-in's visibility. That is the layering machinery. The replaceable part is the reviewed policy's tools.hide (iface:agent.policy/v1), not the assembly.
replaceability.decided: Acrab, 2026-10-24 (assembly stays Lumeri's, also once the code sandbox exists); docs/luc/agent-protocol.md:40-43

operations.name: toolbox_from_official_set

loaded.description: Loaded OfficialLucSet, including safe_mode and migrated_tool_ids. See iface:luc.bootstrap/v1.

operations.notes: No deadline enforced. Returns a live Python Toolbox; definitions describe its declaration projection, while run callables and Host references remain process-local. An empty candidate/readiness/unavailable set returns compatibility directly. Reassembly reads current loaded state and may update readiness withholding.

invariants.text: With the default Official set, declarations contain exactly luc_discover, luc_describe, luc_invoke and use_skill and are English.

break: the operation raises unexpectedly or returns an answer outside its declared schema
failure.notes: No replacement seam or run-time interface validator exists for this role today; the class describes who may eventually replace it.

conformance.notes: Existing tests are evidence for the named invariants, not a replacement conformance runner. Only the area contract checker is run in this task.

known_deviations.text: Safe mode retains the original prompt but loads only recovery Lucs and omits use_skill; the complete request fingerprint differs from the no-layer baseline.

open_questions.text: Should safe mode load all verified originals without layers, or keep the current recovery-only set and its smaller agent toolbox?

toolbox.description: Python Toolbox. tools is a tuple of AgentTool with executable run callbacks; declaration projection is the array defined here, not a serializable Toolbox. See definitions/declarations.
